name: Kagurazaka
tagline: Otemachi in 9 minutes and Tokyo in 15 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 9 minutes to Otemachi, 18 minutes to Shinjuku, 24 minutes to Shibuya and 29 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 24.8 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 23.7 m. The land around the station rises and falls sharply.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 24.8 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 4.9 m to 28.6 m, a difference of 23.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 4 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 2 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 30 clinics and 21 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 神経研究所附属晴和病院, about 12 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is JCHO東京新宿メディカルセンター, about 12 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line runs at 160% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 木場→門前仲町, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000 and 2LDK ¥300,000 to ¥310,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. plenty of places to eat out pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station and a climb from the station to much of the housing holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For how little of the area is in the flood projection, Ushigome-Kagurazaka; for how close the centre is, Kagurazaka.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Kagurazaka. Ushigome-Kagurazaka has the Toei Oedo Line, a different set from Kagurazaka. To Shinagawa, for instance, Ushigome-Kagurazaka takes 4 minutes longer. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, Ushigome-Kagurazaka comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Kagurazaka is ahead on how close the centre is and the number of medical facilities.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Kagurazaka. Edogawabashi has the Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line, a different set from Kagurazaka. To Tokyo, for instance, Edogawabashi takes 5 minutes longer. On the number of medical facilities, Kagurazaka comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People who would rather not walk up and down slopes
People who want another route when service is suspended
noiseSources: 早稲田通り (1 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station rises and falls sharply, and living above or below the slope changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 15 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Tozai Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
